Focused tests, full library suite serially and with four threads, clippy, fmt and the affected differential courts. ASan, Miri, Loom and FRF/SEAL NOT_RUN.
scope: Per-file contract audit of the eight head entries of REMAINING-AUDIT.txt: the indicator callback slot and its holder, the self-test object/callback pair, and the SLH-DSA address blob, FORS signer/verifier, hash context, hash primitives, hypertree and shared key/context layouts. defects.class: transcribed extent derivation (latent out-of-bounds write; authority divergence)
defects.description: SLH_ADRSC_SIZE_TYPECLEAR was derived as SLH_ADRS_SIZE - (SLH_ADRSC_OFF_TYPE + SLH_ADRSC_SIZE_TYPE) = 32 - 10 = 22, so slh_adrsc_set_type_and_clear cleared 22 bytes from offset 10. The authority defines SLH_ADRSC_SIZE_TYPECLEAR as SLH_ADRS_SIZE_TYPECLEAR (slh_adrs.c:35), i.e. 32 - (16 + 4) = 12, the distance from offset 10 to the end of the 22-byte compressed blob. Current callers always pass a 32-byte SlhAdrs, so the extra ten bytes landed in unused tail storage and no reachable OOB occurred; any 22-byte backing buffer, or a compressed address embedded before live data, would have been overwritten.
defects.fix: Define the compressed constant from SLH_ADRS_SIZE_TYPECLEAR exactly as slh_adrs.c:35 does. No call site or ABI changes. Added slh_dsa::tests::the_compressed_address_clear_stays_inside_its_blob, a positive control that fills the backing array with 0xAA and asserts bytes 10..22 are cleared while 22..32 are untouched; it fails on the pre-fix constant.
defects.witness: Authority comparison: forensics/authorities/src/openssl-3.6.4/crypto/slh_dsa/slh_adrs.c:23,35,122-126. The new unit test observes the exact distance and was run in the final BATCH.

defects.class: hidden obligation: safe fn with a caller-validity-dependent raw pointer
defects.description: fors_err was a safe fn taking `wroot_pkt: *mut Wpacket` and calling WPACKET_finish on it. Its safety depended on the caller passing a live, initialised builder, which the safe signature did not express, so a safe caller in the module could have caused UB. The cleanse length was also an unchecked k*n. This is the exact hidden-obligation class the standing standard forbids.
defects.fix: Take `wroot_pkt: &mut Wpacket` and `roots: &mut [u8; SLH_MAX_ROOTS]` instead, deriving liveness from the references, and clamp the cleanse length with saturating_mul/min (inert for every parameter set, where k <= SLH_MAX_K and n <= SLH_MAX_N). The duplicated raw WPACKET_finish/cleanse tail in ossl_slh_fors_pk_from_sig now calls the same safe helper. No unsafe op is introduced and no caller changes.
defects.witness: The helper's only unsafe operations (WPACKET_finish and OPENSSL_cleanse) now have their preconditions established by typed arguments; the crate's Wpacket fields are private and its constructors are unsafe, so a reachable &mut Wpacket is an initialised builder or the zeroed value for which WPACKET_finish returns 0 (packet.rs:800-806).

defects.description: The Safety contracts named ctx and the packet but omitted the readable extents of msg/sk_seed/pk_seed/pk_root and, for ht_sign, the requirement that the signature packet's buffer not move across the XMSS write: psig is taken before the signer runs and reused afterwards. The current caller uses WPACKET_init_static_len over the caller's buffer, so the precondition holds, but it was hidden rather than stated.
defects.fix: State the pointer extents and the non-moving-builder precondition in both Safety contracts. No code, layout or signature change.
defects.witness: dsa.rs:143 initialises sig_wpkt with WPACKET_init_static_len over the caller's sig buffer; packet.rs:419-434 shows that form does not grow.

retained_obligations: slh_dsa/adrs.rs: every accessor requires the address blob to be writable for its own form's size (32 uncompressed, 22 compressed); the methods are reached only through the key's method table.

slh_dsa/fors.rs: slh_base_2b requires (out_len * b + 7) / 8 readable bytes; the tree walk requires the hash/ADRS method tables and every span the arguments name; the secret out/sk/lnode/rnode arrays are cleansed on every return path.

slh_dsa/hash.rs: each primitive requires a live hash context whose key/params and EVP contexts were established by slh_dsa_key_hash_init; secret mac/out/seed locals are cleansed on every return path; hctx.scratch is cleansed by the context's clear-free.
slh_dsa/hypertree.rs: ht_sign requires a non-moving signature builder (now explicit); both functions require msg/pk_seed (and pk_root for verify) readable for n and tree_id/leaf_id within range.
slh_dsa/hash_ctx.rs: .free accepts NULL or a live (possibly partially constructed) context; md_big_ctx may alias md_ctx and is released exactly once; the whole block is clear-freed including scratch.
slh_dsa/mod.rs: SlhDsaKey.priv_ is 4*SLH_DSA_MAX_N bytes and the accessors require a live key with non-NULL params for the n-offset forms; pub_ is an alias into priv_.

selftest/mod.rs and selftest/indicator.rs: the exported callback setters require a NULL or live OSSL_LIB_CTX; the stored callback and cbarg are borrowed, never owned, and must outlive their use; the self-test object's params array aliases its own string fields.
residuals: The compressed ADRS clear fix is a deliberate authority-faithful extent correction; no observable behaviour changes for the crate's 32-byte SlhAdrs buffers.
The SLH-DSA signing code has no constant-time claim; secret-dependent hashing and tree walks were not changed and were not measured.
documentation_corrections: adrs.rs now records that the compressed type-clear extent is the authority's uncompressed formula and why the compressed-offset derivation is wrong.
hypertree.rs now states the full pointer extents and the non-moving signature-builder precondition.
fors.rs's error helper is now a safe function over references rather than a safe-looking raw-pointer function.
shared_boundary_files: src/runtime/bio/owned.rs: CtxDestroy/OwnedCtx/RawCtx reused unmodified; the indicator and self-test holders are all-zero-valid and their destroy bodies release no member.
src/context/mod.rs: lib_ctx_get_data/OSSL_LIB_CTX_get_data reused unmodified; both callback slots continue to take the audited context contract.
src/packet.rs: WPACKET_finish/WPACKET_init_static_len/Packet::buf_init reused unmodified; fors_err now derives the packet precondition from &mut Wpacket.
unsafe_operations_relocated: src/slh_dsa/fors.rs: the duplicate raw WPACKET_finish/OPENSSL_cleanse tail was replaced by the safe fors_err helper; the two unsafe operations are unchanged in count but now live behind typed preconditions.
secret_bearing_buffers: fors.rs: the PRF-generated leaf `sk` is cleansed for n bytes in slh_fors_node; `lnode`/`rnode` are cleansed in full; the secret `out` is cleansed on all three early returns and the success tail of ossl_slh_fors_sign; `roots` is cleansed through fors_err on every exit.

hash.rs: the SHAKE PRFmsg randomizer `out` and the SHA-2 HMAC `mac` (keyed by SK_PRF) are cleansed in full on every return; the SHA-2 H_MSG `seed` (r || pk_seed || digest) is cleansed in full; SHA-2 intermediates in hctx.scratch are cleared when the hash context is freed.
hash_ctx.rs: the whole SlhDsaHashCtx block, including scratch, is released by CRYPTO_clear_free after md_ctx/md_big_ctx (identity-disambiguated) and hmac_ctx are freed.
hypertree.rs: `root` and `node` are cleansed in full on every exit, matching slh_hypertree.c:94,142.

mod.rs: SlhDsaKey.priv_ holds the secret SK_SEED/SK_PRF halves; the already-audited key release in key.rs cleanses sizeof(priv_) >> 1 (64 bytes, covering every n's secret half), and reset/fromdata cleanse the full 128 bytes.
selftest/indicator: no secret contents; only borrowed callback pointers and cb_arg.

boundary_control.name: slh_dsa::tests::the_compressed_address_clear_stays_inside_its_blob
boundary_control.reason: The ADRS extent repair is directly observable: the control fills a 32-byte address with 0xAA and asserts the compressed clear covers offsets 10..22 only. It fails against the pre-fix 22-byte clear and passes against the authority extent. The fors helper's typed arguments make the old failure mode inexpressible, so no separate canary is needed.
